content:
The shmoo formation in *Saccharomyces cerevisiae* is a hallmark of mating pheromone response, during which cells arrest in the G1 phase of the cell cycle and undergo polarized growth to prepare for mating. In this state, DNA replication is halted, and the cell focuses on transcriptional programs necessary for mating. 

The experiment aims to recover the proteome of **active chromatin** (transcriptionally active regions) using chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by mass spectrometry. Active chromatin is typically enriched for proteins involved in transcription and its regulation.

- **(A) Pre-replication complex (pre-RC)**: This complex assembles at origins of replication to license DNA for replication. Since shmoo cells are arrested in G1 and not undergoing DNA replication, and because pre-RC components are associated with replication origins rather than transcriptionally active chromatin, they will be the least abundant in an active chromatin enrichment.
- **(B) Nucleosome histone complex**: Histones are core structural components of all chromatin, both active and inactive, and will be highly abundant.
- **(C) Pre-initiation complex (PIC)**: This transcription machinery assembles at promoters of actively transcribed genes and will be enriched in active chromatin.
- **(D) Enhancer protein complex**: These regulatory proteins (transcription factors) bind to enhancers/UAS elements to drive transcription of active genes and will also be present.

Thus, the pre-replication complex proteins will be the least observed.

Answer: A
